findings.reason: a node built on §2 would implement the range the plan states in §1 and measure no reduction, shipping a repair that leaves the 670k-token estimate intact.
findings.text: §1 prescribes "the three-dot diff against the integration branch, `git diff <base>...HEAD`", but on the cited run the base is itself the merge base, so `<base>...HEAD` returns the identical 160 files and 122,334 insertions as `<base>..HEAD`; the range that actually isolates the run's own work is `origin/main...HEAD`, which returns 6 files and 320 insertions. The sentence's second alternative, "or equivalently the diff of the run's own non-merge commits", is the correct one and is not equivalent — they differ by 154 files.

findings.reason: the control is the only thing that would tell a worker its range change is real, and as written it passes on the unfixed code, so the gate cannot show the guard fires.
findings.text: the negative control, "the same measurement on a run that never merged main gives the same paths under both ranges", is satisfied trivially whenever the compared ranges are `<base>...HEAD` and `<base>..HEAD`, because a base that is an ancestor of the head makes three-dot and two-dot identical — the control holds however the composer behaves and so distinguishes nothing.

findings.reason: the investigation is defined by the sites the worker records and the anchors it gives for them, so a corrected count changes the prose a reader passes over, not the deliverable or its measure.
findings.text: "which of the twelve range sites" asserts a count with no anchor, no list and no source; a grep of `reckon/crew/` and `reckon/clones.py` for two-dot range forms finds six, none of them enumerated in the plan, and the reviewed entries `971`, `1039` and `1091` of `_changed_paths_between` include a call (`reviewed_head..head`) that is not off `base_sha`.

response_events.note: §1 and §2 now name origin/main...HEAD (the run's own commits, 6 files and 320 insertions on the cited run) and drop the base three-dot form, which equals the two-dot range when the base is the merge base
